title: fix(hd256/sm100): make the dedicated hd256 kernel stride-aware (supersede #2666 copy)
body: Fixes #2665. Supersedes the `.contiguous()` stop-gap from #2666. ## Summary The dedicated head_dim=256 SM100 (Blackwell) forward kernel built its q/k/v CuTe layouts with strides synthesized from shape assuming a fully-contiguous BSHD tensor) and reused only the input's base pointer. maybe_contiguous() in the interface only guarantees stride(-1) == 1, so a transpose(1, 2) -ed input — contiguous in the head dim but with swapped sequence/head strides — reached the kernel and produced TMA loads from the wrong addresses, silently corrupting outputs on B200 at `head_dim=256` (#2665). Other head dims and H100 were unaffected because they use kernels that already honor arbitrary input strides. #2666 worked around this by forcing q/k/v contiguous before the kernel, which adds a full copy (~0.4 GB for the issue's `1×32×8192×256` shape) on every forward in the common transposed-input case. **This PR makes the kernel honor the real input strides instead, so the copy is no longer needed.** ## Root cause python # before: strides synthesized from shape, base pointer reused q_layout = cute.make_layout( (s_q_total, d, ((h_r, h_k), b)), stride=(d64 * h_r64 * h_k64, 1, ((d64, d64 * h_r64), stride_b_qo)), # assumes contiguous ) q = cute.make_tensor(q_tensor.iterator, q_layout) This is consistent with how the **general** SM100 forward kernel (`flash_fwd_sm100.py`) and the **hd256 backward** kernels already work — both derive their layouts from the actual tensor strides. The hd256 forward was the only kernel still assuming contiguity. ## Changes - Forward (dense + paged): derive the sequence / head / batch strides from the actual q/k/v tensors for the rank-5, rank-4, and rank-3 (varlen) paths. The `d` (head_dim) mode is kept a **static `1`** — TMA requires the contiguous innermost mode's stride to be statically known, and `maybe_contiguous()` guarantees `stride(-1) == 1`. - Backward: the hd256 backward kernels already derive layouts from real strides, so #2666's backward .contiguous()` was redundant and is removed. - interface.py`: replace the unconditional copy with an **alignment-gated guard** (`maybe_hd256_compatible_contiguous`) that copies only when an input stride would violate the kernel's 16-byte / divby-64 TMA assumptions. This keeps the zero-copy fast path for the common case while staying safe for exotic (e.g. sliced/padded) strides. ## Validation (B200) | Check | Result | |--------|--------| | #2665 repro (transposed, `1×32×8192×256`) | max_abs_err `0.155` → **`4.9e-4`** | | Forward, transposed vs contiguous (same kernel), MHA/GQA/causal | **bit-exact `0.0`** | | Backward, transposed vs contiguous — `out`/`dq`/`dk`/`dv`, MHA/GQA/causal | **bit-exact `0.0`** | | Paged-KV, non-contiguous q (same kernel) | **bit-exact `0.0`** | | Padded-stride fallback (e.g. stride `(…, 257, 1)`) | guard fires, result correct | For a contiguous input the derived strides are arithmetically identical to the old synthesized ones, so the existing supported path is bit-identical to before. ## Test plan - pytest tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py` on the `d=256` slice (forward + backward): **240 passed, 648 skipped** (skips = feature combos hd256 doesn't support: softcap / learnable_sink / local). - ruff check flash_attn/cute/` — clean. - tests ran are summarized in the table below: - ## Notes Developed as two independent implementations that converged on the same design (including the non-obvious TMA static-`1` requirement) and cross-validated each other's results on separate B200s. ## Coauthor: Coauthor: @oattia
